chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Aytham ibn Ashyam, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

One day the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) came out having received good news, smiling with joy. So the people said to him: 'May God keep you smiling, O Messenger of God, and increase your joy.'

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no day or night except that I receive a gift from God in both. Indeed! My Lord has gifted me on this day of mine with a gift the like of which He has never gifted me before. Gabriel came to me and conveyed to me greetings from my Lord, and said: O Muhammad!

God, Mighty and Majestic, has chosen seven from the Clan of Hashim the like of whom He has never created in those who have passed, nor will He create their like among those who remain. You, O Messenger of God, are the Chief of the Prophets; and Ali ibn Abi Talib, your successor, is the Chief of the successors; and al-Hasan and al-Husayn, your two grandsons, are the two Chiefs of the grandsons; and Hamza, your uncle, is the Chief of the martyrs; and Ja'far, the son of your uncle, is the Flyer in Paradise, flying with the angels wherever he pleases; and from among you is the Qa'im behind whom Isa ibn Maryam will pray when God sends him down to the earth — he will be from the descendants of Ali and Fatima, from the children of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.الطَّيَّارُ: The Flyer — the epithet of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who lost both arms at the Battle of Mu'ta and was said to be granted wings in Paradise
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qa'im — the Rising One, a title for the awaited Mahdi in Shia tradition
key_terms.تُحْفَةٌ: Gift — used three times to emphasize the extraordinary nature of the divine bestowal
key_terms.سِبْطَاكَ: Your two grandsons (sibtayk) — specifically referring to al-Hasan and al-Husayn as sons of the Prophet's daughter Fatima
key_terms.وَصِيُّكَ: Your successor/legatee — establishing Ali as the designated successor of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What are the seven chosen ones from Banu Hashim mentioned in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) reported that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) once emerged joyful, and when asked why, he revealed that Gabriel had brought him the greatest gift he had ever received: a divine proclamation naming seven uniquely chosen figures from Banu Hashim. These seven are: the Prophet as Chief of Prophets, Ali ibn Abi Talib as Chief of Successors, al-Hasan and al-Husayn as chiefs of the grandsons, Hamza as Chief of Martyrs, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib as the Flyer in Paradise, and a future Qa'im from the lineage of Ali and Fatima from the children of al-Husayn, behind whom Jesus will pray upon his return. This hadith is significant in the Shia tradition as it establishes the unique cosmic rank of the Ahlulbayt and includes an eschatological reference to the Mahdi.
